You are performing the STANDARDS axis of a two-axis code review. Report only on coding standards and code smells — NOT on whether the change implements its spec (a separate agent covers that).

REPO: /home/moxa/sdc1/home/moxa/SNMP_PLAN_E/buildroot/dl/3rdparty_net_snmp
This is a vendored net-snmp fork (C, embedded, cross-compiled for Cortex-A9 / Marvell CN9130) inside a Buildroot BSP.

DIFF UNDER REVIEW:
  git diff 4b0f050...HEAD
COMMITS:
  2ed5f03 [Plan E Task 3] ies-auto-mibs: keep synthesised index columns local
  aa598f7 [Plan E Task 3] ies-auto-mibs: forward at the local/remote boundary
Files touched: ies-auto-mibs/ies_auto_mibs.c, ies-auto-mibs/moxa_snmp_handle_util.c,
snmp_tools/inc/ies_auto_mibs_handle.h, snmp_tools/inc/ies_common.h

Read the diff AND enough surrounding code to judge context. Note that the surrounding
codebase is old, inconsistent, and full of pre-existing problems — you are reviewing
ONLY what these two commits changed. Do not report pre-existing issues except where a
changed line makes one materially worse.

DOCUMENTED STANDARDS FOR THIS PROJECT (no CODING_STANDARDS.md exists in the repo; these
are the project's stated rules, from the user's CLAUDE.md):
1. Surgical changes: every changed line must trace to the request. Do not "improve"
   adjacent code, do not refactor what is not broken, match existing style even where
   you would do it differently.
2. Simplicity first: minimum code that solves the problem, nothing speculative. No
   abstractions for single-use code, no configurability that was not requested, no
   error handling for impossible scenarios.
3. Clean up only your own mess: remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR change
   made unused; do not delete pre-existing dead code.
4. Source comments must be in English.
5. Match the surrounding file's comment density, naming and idiom.

SMELL BASELINE (Fowler, Refactoring ch.3). These are labelled heuristics, always
judgement calls, never hard violations. A documented repo standard overrides them.
Skip anything tooling already enforces.
- Mysterious Name — a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it
  does or holds. Fix: rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.
- Duplicated Code — the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the
  change. Fix: extract the shared shape, call it from both.
- Feature Envy — a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own.
  Fix: move the method onto the data it envies.
- Data Clumps — the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting
  to be born). Fix: bundle them into one type, pass that.
- Primitive Obsession — a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that
  deserves its own type. Fix: give the concept its own small type.
- Repeated Switches — the same switch/if-cascade on the same type recurs across the
  change. Fix: replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.
- Shotgun Surgery — one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the
  diff. Fix: gather what changes together into one module.
- Divergent Change — one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. Fix:
  split so each module changes for one reason.
- Speculative Generality — abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec
  doesn't have. Fix: delete it; inline back until a real need shows.
- Message Chains — long a.b().c().d() navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. Fix:
  hide the walk behind one method on the first object.
- Middle Man — a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. Fix: cut it, call
  the real target direct.
- Refused Bequest — a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it
  inherits. Fix: drop the inheritance, use composition.

Pay particular attention to things that matter in C on an embedded target and that a
smell list does not cover: control-flow correctness of the restructured if/else chains,
returning an enum value through an int, uninitialised reads, resource leaks (FILE*,
handles) on the new early-return path, and whether a new early return skips cleanup or
timing instrumentation that the old path performed.

BRIEF: Report — per file/hunk where relevant — (a) every place the diff violates a
documented standard: cite the standard (number + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell
you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls.
Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.

## STANDARDS review — Plan E Task 3 (2ed5f03, aa598f7)

### Hard violations

**1. Standard 1 (surgical: every changed line traces to the request)** — `ies_auto_mibs.c:2216`, `ies_handle_t ret = IES_ERR;` in `entry_handle_generate_iss_value_file()`. In that function `ret` is written at 2285 and read at 2286 only; no path reads it uninitialised. The commit message justifies the init by "paths that return `mox_snmp_flask_handle_result(..., ret)`" — that function is never called from the iss generator. The twin init at 2470 in the uri generator *is* a real fix (2527 read it uninitialised); this one traces to nothing.

**2. Standard 1 / 5 (match existing style)** — pure-whitespace churn mixed into the diff: trailing-space strips on `ies_handle_t `, `if ( 0 != clock_gettime(...) ) ` (3302, 3324), and `} `/`else ` reflow at 3309-3310. Several changed lines carry no semantic change.

### Judgement calls

**3. Enum sentinel collides with the SNMP error space — highest risk.** `IES_GET_FORWARDED = 5` was added to `ies_handle_t`, but both generators also return raw SNMP codes through that same return type: `ies_auto_mibs.c:2507` `return SNMP_ERR_BADVALUE;` and 2527/2558/2584/2596/2607 returning `mox_snmp_flask_handle_result()`. `SNMP_ERR_GENERR == 5 == IES_GET_FORWARDED` (and `SNMP_ERR_BADVALUE == 3 == IES_ERR_NOT_FOUND`). No path returns GENERR today, so it doesn't fire — but any future `return SNMP_ERR_GENERR` here is read by the caller (3292/3314) as "forwarded", answering NOERROR with the varbind unfilled. Pre-existing mixed value-space, made live by this change. Cheap fix: sentinel outside 0-5, or a bool out-param.

**4. Per-forwarded-GET global cache wipe.** Moving the forward below `entry_handle_check_value_file()` puts `unlink(fname)` + `util_table_snapshot_reset()` (2277-2278, 2470-2471) ahead of every forwarded GET. `util_table_snapshot_reset()` unlinks and zeroes the single global `gSnmpTblSnapShot` (260-268). In a walk interleaving forwarded and local tables, each forwarded varbind destroys the local table's snapshot → ISS re-read per varbind, not one per 800 ms. The commit message calls this "a redundant ISS read"; it is per-varbind. Measure on the DUT.

**5. Duplicated Code.** The forward guard is verbatim in both generators (2305-2309, 2496-2500) with a near-identical 9-line comment; `if ( IES_GET_FORWARDED == ret ) return SNMP_ERR_NOERROR;` is duplicated at 3292 and 3314.

**6. Divergent Change / Feature Envy.** `entry_handle_generate_*_value_file()` now changes for two reasons — producing a value file and routing the request — and each grew the 3-param net-snmp handler clump used for nothing but the forward.

**7. Standard 5 (comment density).** Surrounding file is near comment-free; the diff adds four multi-line rationale blocks (9/9/7/7 lines) plus a 6-line enum comment, restating the same argument three times.

**8. Instrumentation gap (not a regression).** The `IES_GET_FORWARDED` returns at 3294/3316 skip `util_timeDiff("mib_get_success", ...)` (3349), so forwarded GETs never enter the histogram the "p100 stays at 0.00s" claim is read from. The base commit's top-of-function forward returned early too, so this is inherited — but it caps the evidentiary value of that number.

### Clean

No resource leak on the new early-return paths (`fp2` is closed before 2308; `uri_handle` is created after 2499). Restructured if/else chains in both generators preserve the original branch semantics. Flag array auto-resizes via `IES_SNMP_FLAG_NUM (IES_FLAG_SNMP_MAX/8 + 1)`, so the new enum member cannot overflow `flags[]`. `moxaSnmpHandle_UtilMibEntryCreateIndexEntry()` has exactly one caller, so setting `SYNTHETIC_INDEX` there is not over-broad, and the "must come after the memcpy" comment at `moxa_snmp_handle_util.c:103-105` is accurate.
